message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough. Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order to avoid mistakes. | # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips | |---|------------|----------------|------| | 1 | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) and how much you’re willing to spend. | Use online PC builders (e.g., PCPartPicker) to compare prices and check compatibility. | | 2 | **Gather Tools & Workspace** | A static‑free environment prevents damage. | • 10‑mm Phillips screwdriver
• Anti‑static wrist strap (optional but recommended)
• Clean, flat surface (desk or table). | | 3 | **Choose a Case** | Determines airflow, size, and aesthetics. | ATX mid‑tower is most common; make sure it has enough drive bays and cable‑management options. | | 4 | **Select a Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to all components. | Pick a reputable brand (Corsair, EVGA, Seasonic). 80+ Gold or better, 80+ Platinum if you want efficiency. Calculate wattage:
• CPU: 65‑125 W
• GPU: 200‑350 W (depends on model)
• Others: 50‑100 W
**Rule of thumb:** 500–650 W for mid‑range builds, 750 W+ for high‑end. | | 5 | **Pick a Motherboard** | Connects everything. | Match the socket to your CPU (Intel LGA 1200/1700, AMD AM4/AM5). Check form factor (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX). Verify RAM slots, PCIe lanes, M.2 slots, USB ports, etc. | | 6 | **Choose a CPU** | Core performance. | For gaming: Intel i5/i7 or AMD Ryzen 5/7. For content creation: higher core counts (Ryzen 9, Intel i9). | | 7 | **Get RAM** | Speed & capacity affect multitasking. | 16 GB DDR4/DDR5 is a solid baseline. 32 GB for heavy workloads. Ensure the motherboard supports the speed (e.g., 3200 MHz, 3600 MHz). | | 8 | **Select Storage** | SSDs are faster than HDDs. | • NVMe M.2 SSD (500 GB–1 TB) for OS & games.
• SATA SSD/HDD for bulk storage. | | 9 | **Pick a GPU** | Graphics card for gaming or GPU‑heavy tasks. | Match your monitor’s resolution & refresh rate. For 1080p gaming, mid‑range GPUs (RTX 3060, RX 6600). For 1440p/4K, higher tiers (RTX 3070/3080, RX 6800/6900). | | 10 | **Add Cooling** | Keeps components from overheating. | • Stock cooler (often comes with CPU).
• Aftermarket air cooler (Noctua, be quiet!).
• AIO liquid cooler (240 mm, 280 mm).
• Case fans (intake/outlet). | | 11 | **Prepare the Case** | Remove panels, install standoffs. | • Remove side panel.
• Install standoffs for motherboard (usually pre‑installed). | | 12 | **Install the PSU** | Power first, then everything else. | • Mount PSU in the case (bottom or top).
• Route cables neatly. | | 13 | **Mount the Motherboard** | Align with standoffs and I/O shield. | • Insert I/O shield into rear cut‑out.
• Align motherboard holes with standoffs.
• Secure with screws. | | 14 | **Install CPU** | Handle with care. | • Open CPU socket latch.
• Align CPU (triangle marker).
• Gently place, lock latch. | | 15 | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install Cooler** | Ensures heat transfer. | • Small pea‑size amount on CPU center.
• Attach cooler per manufacturer instructions. | | 16 | **Insert RAM** | Slot into DIMM slots. | • Open latch, align notch, press firmly until clicks. | | 17 | **Mount Storage** | SSDs in M.2 slot or 2.5″ bay. | • For M.2: insert at 30° angle, screw down.
• For 2.5″: slide into bay, secure with screws. | | 18 | **Install GPU** | PCIe slot. | • Remove slot cover.
• Align with slot, push until fully seated.
• Secure with screw. | | 19 | **Connect Power Cables** | PSU to motherboard, GPU, storage, fans. | • 24‑pin ATX, 8‑pin EPS for CPU, 6/8‑pin PCIe for GPU, SATA power for drives, 4‑pin fan connectors. | | 20 | **Cable Management** | Improves airflow & aesthetics. | • Tuck cables behind motherboard tray.
• Use zip ties or Velcro straps. | | 21 | **Check Connections** | Double‑check all cables. | • Ensure no loose screws or cables blocking fans. | | 22 | **Close the Case** | Replace side panel, secure screws. | • Don’t overtighten; leave a little wiggle for future maintenance. | | 23 | **First Boot** | Power on, enter BIOS. | • Press power button.
• If nothing happens, double‑check PSU switch, cables, and that the case button is connected. | | 24 | **Enter BIOS/UEFI** | Verify component detection. | • Check CPU, RAM, storage, GPU appear.
• Set boot priority to your OS drive. | | 25 | **Install Operating System** | Windows, Linux, etc. | • Create bootable USB (Rufus, BalenaEtcher).
• Follow on‑screen prompts. | | 26 | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Ensure hardware works. | • Install motherboard chipset drivers.
• GPU drivers (NVIDIA GeForce Experience, AMD Radeon Software).
• Update Windows or Linux kernel. | | 27 | **Test Performance** | Run benchmarks, stress tests. | • 3DMark, Cinebench, Prime95, MemTest86. | | 28 | **Fine‑Tune Settings** | Overclocking, fan curves, RGB lighting. | • Use BIOS or software (MSI Afterburner, ASUS AI Suite). | | 29 | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Keep dust‑free, update drivers. | • Clean fans every 3–6 months.
• Monitor temperatures (HWMonitor, SpeedFan). | --- #### Quick Checklist (Before You Start) - [ ] Case, PSU, motherboard, CPU, RAM, GPU, storage, cooling, cables, screws, standoffs. - [ ] Anti‑static wrist strap or anti‑static mat. - [ ] Screwdriver set (Phillips #2, #0, #1). - [ ] Thermal paste (if not pre‑applied). - [ ] USB drive with OS installer. - [ ] Internet connection for driver downloads. #### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them | Issue | Fix | |-------|-----| | **CPU not seated** | Double‑check alignment, ensure latch is fully locked. | | **GPU not recognized** | Make sure it’s fully inserted, power cables attached. | | **No POST** | Verify PSU switch on, all cables connected, no shorting. | | **Overheating** | Reapply thermal paste, improve cable management, add case fans. | | **Fan noise** | Tighten screws, replace noisy fans, adjust fan curves. | --- ### Resources - **PCPartPicker** – Build planner, price comparison, compatibility checker. - **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware. - **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community help. - **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, PSU, and GPU manuals for specific instructions. Happy building! If you hit a snag, let me know which step and I’ll help troubleshoot.
message.reasoning: User asks: "How to build a new PC?" They want instructions. We can provide a step-by-step guide. No need to fetch recipe. Just give instructions.
